title: procurement-playbook-risk-ladders-and-fallbacks-dedicated
body:
Purpose:
Quick-reference playbook for procurement and platform-eng conversations that need: a clear risk ladder (what happens when capacity/latency degrades), buyer-friendly fallbacks (technical and commercial), and contract language snippets that map to our technical guardrails.

Audience:
- Procurement / Legal (negotiating terms)
- Platform & Infra architects (validating fallbacks)
- Sales AE / Solutions (deal-level positioning + objection handling)

High-level thesis (one-liner):
Buyers want predictability. We sell a combination of throughput guarantees + operational escape hatches (both automated and contractual) that preserve availability and degrade gracefully when capacity is constrained.

Core messaging pillars (short):
1) Predictable throughput — SLOs tied to committed GPU pools and configurable burst policies.
2) Isolation guarantees — tenant isolation surface and measurable interference controls.
3) Graceful fallback ladder — automated model/region/queue fallbacks + commercial credits & rapid remediation.
4) Transparent remediation — post-incident reports, cost/latency breakout, and rewindable audit trails.

Risk ladder (operational states + buyer-facing outcome):
- Green: Committed capacity meets SLO (normal operations).
- Yellow: Degraded but acceptable — throughput reduced, latency p95 targets missed by <20%, auto-burst invoked. Customer receives real-time alert + retry hints.
- Orange: Material degradation — queued requests, automatic model downgrade to compatible variant (quantized or shorter context), targeted rate-limiting, dedicated support page and SLA credit path.
- Red: Severe outage — automatic regional reroute to secondary capacity or hosted fallback model, defined credit formula + incident RCA within 72 hours.

Suggested technical fallbacks (order of application):
1) Prefix/KV cache warm-up: prioritize cached KV hits to preserve low-latency interactive flows.
2) Dynamic batching window adjust: slightly increase batching thresholds for throughput critical flows (configurable).
3) Model variant downgrade: switch to pre-approved quantized or distilled variant with documented quality delta.
4) Regional redirect: route traffic to failover region with capacity buffer (if contractual).
5) Hosted fallback route: fall back to hosted multi-tenant endpoint with limited throughput but maintained availability.
6) Degraded feature flags: toggle non-essential augmentations (e.g., long-context analysis, secondary rerankers).

Commercial fallback constructs (for contracts):
- Burst bucket: limited, billable burst capacity on top of committed baseline (clear pricing + cooldown rules).
- SLA credits ladder: credits scale with severity (p95 latency bands, throughput shortfall percent).
- Termination/escape clause: right to terminate or re-negotiate on repeated breaches (e.g., >3 breaches in 12 months).
- Price protection for migrations: if buyer is forced to move to alternate provider due to repeated breaches, limit future price escalation for a fixed window.

Negotiation talking points (short scripts):
- Procurement concern: "What if you run out of GPUs during our launch?"
  Response: "We operate dedicated pools with configurable burst and failover policies. For launches we recommend a short-term burst commitment and can map pre-approved model downgrades to preserve availability. If the baseline isn't met, our SLA credit ladder and termination path provide commercial protection."

- Platform concern: "How do we preserve tail-latency for interactive users?"
  Response: "We prioritize KV/cache hits and provide a latency-priority routing policy at the edge. We can pin high-priority routes to an ultra-low-latency pool within your reserved capacity and apply size-limited bursts for launches."

Competitive differentiators to call out (straightbat):
- We provide both the deep observability (per-route token cost + latency attribution) and the operational primitives (model variant plumbing, autoscaling policies) in a single contract — not an integration of multiple vendors.
- Our fallback ladder is codified into Rollouts/Policies in the console so ops can onboard the same behaviors used for production failovers.
- Commercial terms are aligned with technical controls (e.g., explicit price for hosting fallback routes, documented quality deltas for each model variant).

Rebuttals to common procurement objections:
- "We need absolute isolation": We offer dedicated capacity with audit logs, KMS integration and optional single-tenant control plane for regulated workloads. For absolute physical separation ask for Dedicated+ (on-prem/colocated option) — map to private-deploy pricing.
- "We want unlimited burst": Unlimited burst increases cost+risk for both parties; instead propose a bounded burst bucket with usage caps and cooldowns visible in billing.
- "What about model drift if you downgrade?": We provide pre-evalled variant matrices (accuracy vs latency) and a changelog per model variant. Include acceptance tests in the contract (small prompt suite) to validate quality for critical flows.

Suggested SLA language snippets (short, procurement-ready):
- Throughput SLA: "Provider will maintain average committed throughput of X tokens/s per reserved pool over any 24-hour window. If average throughput falls below 95% of committed for >4 hours, customer may claim SLA credit as specified in Appendix A."
- Latency SLA: "Provider will maintain p95 inference latency < Y ms for requests routed to dedicated pool under steady-state conditions (excluding burst windows). Credit bands: 95–110%: 10% credit, 110–150%: 30% credit, >150%: 70% credit."
- Isolation & Security: "Provider will ensure tenant isolation via dedicated GPU pools and network segmentation. Provider will provide audit logs and KMS-integrated key management for customer-controlled encryption."
- Remediation & RCA: "Provider will issue a preliminary incident summary within 8 hours and a full RCA within 72 hours for any outage that triggered a credit."

Appendix A — Example credit table (simple):
- Minor (yellow): single-day throughput shortfall up to 10% = 5% monthly credit
- Material (orange): sustained shortfall 10–30% over 24h = 20% monthly credit
- Severe (red): shortfall >30% or outage = 50–100% credits depending on duration

Procurement checklist (what to ask for in early RFP/RFI):
- Explicit committed throughput value + measurement method
- Defined burst bucket size & pricing
- Model variant catalog + quality deltas + acceptance tests
- Incident SLAs and RCA timelines
- Audit logs and KMS/HSM options
- Failover region availability and latency delta estimates
- Sample contract clauses for termination and credits

Open questions / items to finalize (internal):
- Define standard quantized/downgraded variant names and turnkey quality delta matrix (Maya to own).
- Burst pricing tiers: finalize three common templates (small, medium, launch) and map to pricing (Diego).
- Legal: propose a default termination threshold to use in sales docs (Samir).

Quick implementation notes for Solutions Eng:
- Create a "launch kit" that bundles a short-term burst offer + pre-approved downgrade plan + acceptance prompt-suite.
- Include a console toggle called "aggressive-fallback" that automates model downgrade + hosted fallback route when triggered; surface as a checkbox in sales quotes.

Useful links / context (internal):
- Slack thread: #prod-inference-fallbacks (see pinned discussion Nov 2025)
- Confluence page: GTMP/Dedicated-SLA-Patterns (link above)
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-4921 (coverage for burst-bandwidth metrics)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep contract language modular so sales can mix-and-match burst vs. failover vs. premium isolation.
- Avoid "unlimited" in any customer-facing doc. Use bounded guarantees + transparent monitoring.

Status: draft -> need feedback from Legal on proposed credit bands and from Applied-ML on realistic quality deltas for variant downgrades.
